extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians, researchers, and programmers using Singular)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the 'Data types' chapter of the Singular manual describing types (bigintmat, int, intmat, intvec, ideal, links, etc.), their syntax, semantics, operations, casts, and related functions, with examples and notes. Intended to guide correct usage and behaviors in Singular code.

rubrics_metrics.name: bigintmat type cast
rubrics_metrics.description: bigintmat ( expression ) — Converts expression to a bigintmat, where expression must be of type intmat, or bigintmat. The size (resp. dimension) of the created bigintmat equals the size (resp. dimension) of the expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: bigintmat(im) casts an intmat im to bigintmat; bigintmat(intmat(intvec(...))) shows chained casts. Cross-references: Section 3.5.5 [Type conversion and casting], Section 4.3 [bigintmat], Section 4.7.3 [intmat type cast].

rubrics_metrics.name: bigintmat operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the arithmetic and access operations available on bigintmat objects: +, -, *, comparators (<>, ==), indexing and entry access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics: addition/subtraction/multiplication defined with intmat, int, or bigint (scalars act entrywise); negation/subtraction with int subtracts from every entry; multiplication by (big-)int multiplies every entry. Indexing: bigintmat expression [ int, int ] yields entry (row, col). Examples: m*3 multiplies each entry by 3; m[1,3] accesses entry. Error: incompatible types give error (example shown). See related sections for casting and type conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: def (untyped object definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects may be defined without a specific type: they inherit their type from the first assignment to them. Syntax: def name = expression ; Purpose: defines an object of the same type as the right-hand side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: For rings, def creates another reference (alias) to the same ring (not a copy), so entries in one ring appear also in the other. Useful when the basering is not local to a procedure but a local name is needed. Example: def j = i^2; def s = basering; setring s; nameof(basering) → s. Cross-reference: typeof.

rubrics_metrics.name: def declarations (syntax and purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: def name = expression ; Purpose: deﬁnes an object of the same type as the right-hand side. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use-case: right-hand side may be of variable type due to computation (ideal, module, matrix). Also used in procedures to give the basering a name local to the procedure. Example: def i=2; typeof(i) → int.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal (representation and basering dependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideals are represented as lists of polynomials which generate the ideal. They can only be defined or accessed with respect to a basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: size counts only non-zero generators while ncols counts all generators. Many ideal operations and functions depend on basering. Examples provided throughout (defining ideals, generators). Cross-references: many Section 5.1 functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: ideal name = list of poly and ideal expressions ; or ideal name = ideal expression ; Purpose: deﬁnes an ideal. Default: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ideal i = s1, s2-s1, 0, s2*s3, s3^4; i; size(i) → counts non-zero generators. Use list syntax and simplification behaviors are illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal expressions (what constitutes one)
rubrics_metrics.description: An ideal expression is: (1) an identifier of type ideal; (2) a function returning an ideal; (3) a combination of ideal expressions by + or *; (4) a power of an ideal expression (^ or **); (5) a type cast to ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: product i*i involves all products of generators; i^2 involves only different ones (faster). Example: ideal m = maxideal(1); ideal j = ideal(v) where v is a vector. Cross-reference: type casts to ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported operations on ideals: + (addition/concatenation of generators with simplification), * (multiplication with ideal, poly, vector, module with simplification in case of ideal*ideal), ^ (exponentiation by non-negative integer), and indexing ideal expression [ int, int ] to get polynomial generators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate simplification (I + 0 → _[1]=1), multiplication behavior (I * J), use with vectors and modules. Note on simplification: see simplify. Example shows ncols and size differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: ideal related functions (catalog)
rubrics_metrics.description: A long list of functions applicable to ideals (and related computations): char_series, coeffs, contract, diff, degree, dim, eliminate, facstd, factorize, fglm, finduni, fres, groebner, highcorner, homog, hilb, indepSet, interred, intersect, jacob, jet, kbase, koszul, lead, lift, liftstd, lres, maxideal, minbase, minor, modulo, mres, mstd, mult, ncols, nres, preimage, qhweight, quotient, reduce, res, simplify, size, slimgb, sortvec, sres, std, stdfglm, stdhilb, subst, syz, vdim, weight, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each listed function has its own detailed reference elsewhere (cross-references to specific Section 5.1 entries and page numbers given). Short descriptions included for many (e.g., hilb → Hilbert series; mult → multiplicity). Use this list to locate ideal-related functionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: int (machine integers semantics and uses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables of type int represent the machine integers and are limited in range (e.g., -2147483647..2147483647 on 32-bit machines). They are mainly used to count things, in loops, and to represent boolean values (FALSE is 0, any other value TRUE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integers are sequences of digits maybe preceded by sign; spaces not allowed between digits. Values outside range are converted to bigint (or number when a basering is defined). Use int for counters, indexing, boolean tests. See limitations section if range too small (use number over char 0 ring).

rubrics_metrics.name: int declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: int name = int expression ; Purpose: defines an integer variable. Default: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: int i = 42; int j = i + 3; int k; k; → 0. Assignment and arithmetic examples provided. Cross-reference: 3.5.5 Type conversion and casting; 4.14 number.

rubrics_metrics.name: int expressions (what is allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: An int expression can be: (1) a sequence of digits (converted to bigint if too large), (2) an identifier of type int, (3) a function returning int, (4) an expression involving ints and +,-,*,div,%,^, (5) a boolean expression, (6) a type cast to int.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show overflow behavior, automatic conversion to bigint, and use of type cast number for larger range. Cross-reference: Section 6.1 Limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: int operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: ++ (increment), -- (decrement) but these are not int expressions (can't be assigned); +, -, *, div, %, ^, comparators (<, >, <=, >=, ==, <>) are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important note: j = i++; is not allowed (right side is not a datum), so ++/-- do not return a value as in C. Examples illustrate increments, arithmetic, div/mod semantics (div rounds toward 0), and negative mod behavior. See limitations for assignment caveat.

rubrics_metrics.name: int related functions (catalog)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions related to ints and numeric computations: char, deg, det, dim, extgcd, find, gcd, koszul, memory, mult, ncols, npars, nrows, nvars, ord, par, pardeg, prime, random, regularity, rvar, size, trace, var, vdim, weight, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short descriptors included for many (e.g., prime → next lower prime). Each function cross-referenced to Section 5.1 entries in manual for detailed semantics and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean expressions (semantics and comparison rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: A boolean expression is an int expression used in a logical context: any int expression <> 0 evaluates to TRUE (1), 0 evaluates to FALSE (0). Provides comparison lists for integers, numbers, polynomials/vectors (comparisons on leading term), intmat/matrix, intvec/string (lexicographic), and compositions via and/or/not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: no comparisons exist for ideals and modules, resolutions and maps. For finite fields and field extensions, some comparisons behave specially (0 smallest, Z/p representatives in range, >=/<= behave differently). Evaluation strategy: all arguments of a logical expression are first evaluated (no short-circuit). This differs from C's left-to-right conditional evaluation. Cross-reference: Major differences to C programming language.

rubrics_metrics.name: boolean operations (operators and precedence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Boolean operators: and (also &&), or (also ||), not (also !). Precedence order: parentheses, comparisons, not, and, or.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate precedence and explicit parentheses. Example: (1>2) and 3 → 0. Note that 1||b in other languages short-circuits but here both operands are evaluated first.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat (integer matrices overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integer matrices (intmat) are matrices with integer entries; they don't belong to a ring and can be defined without a basering. An intmat can be multiplied by and added to an int (int converted to diagonal intmat). The integer 1 is converted to the unit matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Range limitations of ints apply. Examples show filling rules, submatrix extraction, multiplication with vectors, and trace/determinant usage. See intmat declarations and operations for syntax and semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat declarations (syntax and filling rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: intmat name = intmat expression ; intmat name [ rows ] [ cols ] = intmat expression ; intmat name [ rows ] [ cols ] = list of int and intvec and intmat expressions ; rows and cols must be positive int expressions. Purpose: defines an intmat variable. Default: 0 (1x1 matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a list of integers, the matrix is filled row-major left-to-right; if fewer than rows*cols elements, filled with zeros; if more, only first rows*cols used. Examples: intmat im[3][5]=1,3,...; submatrix examples shown using slicing.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat expressions (what forms intmat expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: An intmat expression is: (1) an identifier of type intmat, (2) a function returning intmat, (3) an intmat operation involving ints and int operations, (4) an expression involving intmats and operations (+,-,*), (5) a type cast to intmat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Idm + 1 (adds unit matrix), transpose(m2), assigning intvec rows to build a matrix, trace(m1*m2). Cross-reference: Type conversion and casting.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat type cast
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: intmat ( expression ) or intmat ( expression, int n, int m ). Purpose: Converts expression to an intmat, where expression must be of type intvec, intmat, or bigintmat. Optional n,m specify dimensions; otherwise inferred. If bigint entry exceeds int limit, set to 0 in returned intmat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: intmat(intvec(1)), intmat(intvec(1),1,2), intmat(intvec(...),2,2). Casting from bigintmat shows overflow-to-0 behavior. Cross-references: Type conversion section, bigintmat, matrix type cast.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Supported operations: +, -, *, div, /, %, mod, comparators ( <>, == ), indexing via intmat expression [ intvec expression, intvec expression ].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics: + and - with intmat or int (int is converted to diagonal intmat), * with intmat/intvec/int (int to diagonal), div performs integer division entrywise (omit remainder), %/mod is entrywise modulo. Indexing returns entry at (row,col). Examples show multiplication, transpose, %2, div2, slicing, size, nrows/ncols.

rubrics_metrics.name: intmat related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions applicable to intmat: betti, det, ncols, nrows, random (pseudo random intmat), size, transpose, trace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function cross-referenced to its Section 5.1 entry. Examples: det(m) returns determinant; transpose returns transpose; size returns total number of entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: intvec (integer vectors overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variables of type intvec are lists of integers. They may simulate sets of integers (or act as index sets). Addition and subtraction with ints or intvecs is element-wise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Range is limited by int. intvecs are ordered lists; many operations and conversions with intmat and other types exist. Examples show concatenation, repetition, range construction, and using intvec as indices for matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: intvec declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: intvec name = intvec expression ; intvec name = list of int and intvec expressions ; Purpose: defines an intvec variable. Default: 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: intvec iv=1,3,5,7,8; indexing iv[4] → 7; slicing iv[3..size(iv)] → 5 7 8. Use repeated-entry syntax a:b to create repeated intvec entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: intvec expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: An intvec expression is: (1) a range int..int, (2) a repeated entry int:positive_int, (3) a function returning intvec, (4) expression involving intvec operations with int (+,-,*,/,% ), (5) expressions of intvecs involving +, -, (6) intvec operation with intmat (*), (7) a type cast to intvec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concatenation and repetition examples: v = 7:k where k=3 yields 7,7,7. Using intvec as indices on intmat: m*v yields intvec. leadexp(f) returns exponent vector as intvec.

rubrics_metrics.name: intvec operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations: +, -, * (with intvec or int, component-wise), / div, %, mod (component-wise), comparisons ( <>, ==, <=, >=, >, < ) lexicographically with shorter lengths padded with zeros, indexing intvec expression [ int expression ] gets element (1-based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: iv+1 adds 1 to each entry; iv*2 multiplies; iv div 2 does component-wise integer division; iv + iv does element-wise addition with padding; iv[iw] uses intvec iw as index vector. Cross-reference: size, sortvec.

rubrics_metrics.name: intvec related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions related to intvec: hilb, indepSet, leadexp, monomial, nrows, qhweight, size, sortvec, transpose (returns intmat), weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short descriptions: leadexp → exponent vector of leading monomial; hilb → Hilbert series as intvec. Each function cross-referenced to Section 5.1 entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: link (communication channels overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Links are communication channels in Singular; Singular supports ASCII links, ssi links, pipe links, and DBM links. Syntax for declaration: link name = string expression ; Purpose: defines a new communication link. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links allow read/write to files, other processes, TCP sockets, or DBM. Examples show creating ASCII link ":w example.txt" and writing/reading. Cross-reference: detailed subsections for ASCII, ssi, pipe, DBM links.

rubrics_metrics.name: link declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Syntax: link name = string expression ; Purpose: defines a new communication link. Default: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: link l=":w example.txt"; write(l,s,i); close(l); read(l); The string describes type and name; status(l) can be used to inspect link properties such as type, mode, open/read/write readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: link expressions (format of link-describing string)
rubrics_metrics.description: A link expression is either an identifier of type link or a string describing the link: property string followed by name string. Property string describes link type (ASCII, ssi, DBM) and mode (read, write, append).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed formats defer to specific link types: ASCII (4.9.4), ssi (4.9.5), pipe (4.9.6), DBM (4.9.7). The link description controls behavior (e.g., "ASCII:r filename" opens for reading).

rubrics_metrics.name: link related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions: close, dump, getdump, open, read, status, write, kill, waitall, waitfirst. These manage opening/closing, reading/writing, dumping variables, and synchronization of links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each function cross-referenced to its Section 5.1 entry. Example: status(l,"open","yes") checks if link is open; write(l,...) writes expressions; read(l) reads expressions (ASCII returns string, ssi returns expressions).

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII links (format and semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASCII links write data convertible to string into files or other processes in plain ASCII format. The ASCII link describing string can be "ASCII:filename", "ASCII:r filename", "ASCII:w filename", or "ASCII:a filename". Defaults: type ASCII may be omitted; mode set by first read/write; omitted filename means stdin/stdout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Reading returns a string (user must parse if needed). ASCII links cannot be used for both reading and writing concurrently; close required before direction change. Note: types without conversion to string cannot be written. Example workflow: link l=":w example.txt"; write(l,1,";",2,...); close(l); read("example.txt") returns strings appended.
Formatting of polynomial output follows global variable short. execute(read(l)) can execute returned strings as commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ssi links (purpose and modes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ssi (simple singular interface) links enable fast storage and communication of Singular data between Singular processes. Data is exchanged in evaluated expression form (not strings) and, for ring-dependent data, ring descriptions are included. Ssi links can be file-based or TCP-based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading from an ssi link returns expressions (not strings) and may change the current ring if the expression is from a different ring (the read sets current ring). Not everything implemented; under development note present. Use ssi for faster binary-style exchange and when preserving expression structure is desired over ASCII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ssi file links (syntax and behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ssi file links use ssi formatted files for efficient storage. Describing strings: "ssi:r filename", "ssi:w filename", "ssi:a filename" for read/overwrite/append. Ssi file links can be used either for reading or writing (not both), and close before direction change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading returns expressions one at a time (not strings). Example: link l="ssi:w example.ssi"; write(l,1, i, "hello world"); close(l); then reading returns expressions in order; read may assign basering from data and create new names. Example shows that reading may set current ring and create variables accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ssi tcp links (modes and launch semantics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ssi tcp links allow data exchange between Singular processes over TCP (same/different hosts). Modes: tcp (Singular acts as server), connect (client), tcp <host>:<program> (client launching app via ssh), fork (forks another Singular acting as server).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describing strings: "ssi:tcp" (server waits at first free port >1024), "ssi:connect host:port" (client connect), "ssi:tcp"+host:application (launch mode via ssh), "ssi:fork" (fork on same host). In launch mode, the launched application must be in PATH or given by absolute pathname; fork mode inherits variables/values into child. Client waits for server application to connect (listening at free port).
